# HUptimeHistory

> Duration-weighted status intervals with explicit unknown coverage and interval inspection.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.10.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HUptimeHistory` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-uptime-history>`.
- Constructor: `HearthUptimeHistoryElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Diagrams.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HUptimeHistory.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- start/end are numeric positions in one shared unit; label supplies human-readable timestamps. Widths encode durations and gaps remain unknown. Up percentage excludes unknown time; unknown coverage is reported separately. Overlaps suppress the availability calculation. Invalid/nonpositive intervals are omitted. A native select and interval table make every narrow interval accessible. maxIntervals defaults to 240 (maximum 1000).

## Public API

intervals: UptimeInterval[] · label, unit, selected: string · maxIntervals: number

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    label: string;
    intervals: UptimeInterval[];
    unit?: string;
    maxIntervals?: number;
    selected?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ intervals: () => [], unit: "ms", maxIntervals: 240 }
```

### Events

select(string)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        id: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, strip, control

Use `hearth-uptime-history::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface UptimeInterval {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    start: number;
    end: number;
    status: UptimeStatus;
}

export type UptimeStatus = "up" | "degraded" | "down" | "unknown";
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HUptimeHistory } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HUptimeHistory label="API availability" unit="minutes" :intervals="[{id:'a',label:'09:00–09:30',start:0,end:30,status:'up'},{id:'b',label:'09:30–09:35',start:30,end:35,status:'down'},{id:'c',label:'09:40–10:00',start:40,end:60,status:'up'}]" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-uptime-history');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "API availability",
  "unit": "minutes",
  "intervals": [
    {
      "id": "a",
      "label": "09:00–09:30",
      "start": 0,
      "end": 30,
      "status": "up"
    },
    {
      "id": "b",
      "label": "09:30–09:35",
      "start": 30,
      "end": 35,
      "status": "down"
    },
    {
      "id": "c",
      "label": "09:40–10:00",
      "start": 40,
      "end": 60,
      "status": "up"
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('select', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
